answer: Bind each agent identity to a hardware attestation key: a secure enclave signs a one-per-device certificate, and the network only admits identities whose key proves a real chip backs it. Like a single narrow inlet admitting one ship at a time, onboarding becomes a physical bottleneck. A Sybil farmer who wants a thousand fake agents must buy a thousand devices, each voyage of fabrication costing real money, while an onyx-hard ledger records every certificate so duplicates are spotted instantly. The attack stops being free software and becomes an expensive hardware bill.
